cards.q: What is a safe following distance?
cards.a: At least three seconds in good weather. Increase the gap in rain, darkness and icy conditions.

cards.q: What does a triangular sign mean?
cards.a: Warning: there is a hazard or a change in conditions ahead.

cards.q: What does a round sign mean?
cards.a: Prohibition, obligation or restriction, such as a speed limit.

cards.q: What should you do at a stop sign?
cards.a: Stop completely, check both directions and only then move off when it is safe.

cards.q: What is the blind spot?
cards.a: The area the mirrors do not cover. That is why you must glance over your shoulder before changing lane.

cards.q: In what order do you check before changing lane?
cards.a: Mirror, then over your shoulder, then indicate in good time – and then change lane.

cards.q: What should you do when entering a roundabout?
cards.a: Slow down, give way to those already inside it and choose your lane early.

cards.q: When do you signal when leaving a roundabout?
cards.a: In good time, before you leave the roundabout.

cards.q: How do you best join a motorway?
cards.a: Use the slip road to build speed and match the traffic, then check your mirror and look over your shoulder.

cards.q: Which lane should you be in on a motorway?
cards.a: The right-hand lane when you are not overtaking.

cards.q: What should you check before setting off?
cards.a: Seat, mirrors, seat belts, lights, wipers and that the windows are clean.

cards.q: May you use your phone while driving?
cards.a: Not unless it is hands-free – even a short message takes your attention off the road.

cards.q: What should you do in the dark?
cards.a: Use your lights, keep the windows clean, drive more slowly and look further ahead.

cards.q: What should you do on a wet or icy road?
cards.a: Increase the distance, reduce speed and brake gently and earlier than usual.

cards.q: What is defensive driving?
cards.a: Seeing hazards in advance, looking far ahead, allowing for other people's mistakes and always having an escape route.

cards.q: How far ahead should you look?
cards.a: About 12–15 seconds along the road.

cards.q: What is a common mistake in a roundabout?
cards.a: Entering too fast and deciding too late which exit to take.

cards.q: What is assessed in the driving test?
cards.a: Safe and steady driving, observation, roundabouts, speed control, understanding of signs and communication in traffic.

cards.q: What should you do before the driving test?
cards.a: Go over the material and the checklist, check the car, arrive on time with your documents and rest well.

cards.q: May you drive faster than the speed limit?
cards.a: No. The speed limit is a ceiling, not a target – your speed must always suit the conditions.

cards.q: What should you do if something unexpected happens in the car?
cards.a: Stop in a safe place before making a decision.

cards.q: What should you do when a car is pulling out of a side road?
cards.a: Give yourself room and keep an escape route in case it does not give way.

cards.q: What is good to do after every lesson?
cards.a: Go over what went well, what needs more practice and book the next lesson.

cards.q: What matters in communication with other road users?
cards.a: Clear signals in good time, consideration and allowing for other people's mistakes.
